open_questions: Odd/even folded 1.67 d signal shows 28% depth difference; RV at ~3.34 d is needed to rule out an EB at twice the period versus two spot phases causing alternating depths.
Depth drops from 2663 ppm in sector 4 to 1459 ppm in sector 31 within TESS-SPOC; simultaneous multi-colour transit photometry would test spot dilution versus baseline drift.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 1.7-day, ~2500 ppm flat-bottomed dip centred on the star with no nearby star able to mimic it and a size of about 3 Earth radii. The dip changes depth between sectors and alternates odd/even, but the star varies strongly at the same period, indicating spot activity is distorting the signal. A hot gas giant with a tiny secondary and off-target centroid is disfavoured, so the planet explanation remains best.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target; all neighbours that could fake it are 25+ sigma from the centroid.
No star inside a TESS pixel can produce the 2545 ppm dip with <=25% eclipse.
Flat-bottomed, near-central-duration dip favours a planet over a grazing/V-shaped binary.
Planet-sized; even with larger Gaia radius it remains well below the stellar regime.

Odd/even depths differ (2023 vs 2842 ppm) and sector_oe_max_sigma 5.742 argues for an EB at twice the period, but on_target centroid, no secondary (snr 1.635), no phase-curve or density match, size below stellar, and changing depth within a single pipeline point to diluted/stochastic variability on an M dwarf rather than a stellar companion.

Large spot modulation at the orbital period and a large stellar-density penalty favour a spotted active star, consistent with the sector depth change (sectors.p_constant 8.736e-7, sectors depth 2663 vs 1459 ppm, sector_depths_by_source changes_within_a_source) and not with a close binary.
